prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production sprite animation atlas for a gritty modern-war 2D side-scrolling pixel game. Create ONE transparent-background sprite sheet EXACTLY 8 columns by 4 rows: 32 separate full-body adult soldier DIGGING animation sprites. Suggested canvas 2048x1024. No titles, labels, letters, borders, guide lines or visible checkerboard: real transparent alpha. Every cell same size with generous empty margins. Read the 8-step digging cycle left to right, repeat it with four different soldier identities, one identity per row. Side view facing RIGHT. Same exact low kneeling planted feet in all 8 frames, torso and both arms move through an actual continuous shovel cycle. A short entrenching spade, held with BOTH hands separated along the shaft; a rifle is securely slung on the back, NEVER held during digging. Real adult proportions (normal small helmet/head, long adult limbs, no chibi, toy, bobblehead or cartoon infant). Detailed deliberate hard square pixel clusters, restrained olive/khaki/charcoal colors, similar to realistic pixel soldier game sprites, no soft painted blur, no smooth vector shapes, no outlines thicker than one pixel at native game scale.
Rows: 1 regular infantry in olive camouflage helmet, flak vest, olive pack; 2 marine in tan helmet with dark goggles, dusty sand/olive field uniform and tan webbing; 3 armed police in dark navy uniform with black tactical helmet and vest, no riot shield, no lettering; 4 militia in brown knit cap, plain brown jacket, olive trousers, small canvas satchel. Keep each identity consistent from frame to frame.
Columns must depict visibly DIFFERENT shovel angles and arm/body poses, not duplicate images:
1 READY: one knee down, other boot planted forward, back upright but slightly bent, both hands hold spade diagonally downward forward, blade just above soil level.
2 REACH: lean torso forward, extend elbows, shovel blade farther forward almost touching ground; top hand nearer knee.
3 DRIVE: shoulders low and forward, downward pressure with both hands, blade at ground, shaft near vertical and hands visibly lower; boot and grounded knee remain planted.
4 LEVER: lean back slightly, bend elbows, shovel tilts upward with a small brown clod visibly on blade lifted a little from ground.
5 LIFT: torso recovers upward, both elbows flex, loaded shovel held horizontally at waist, small soil clod on blade clearly lifted.
6 THROW: twist upper torso slightly, extend both arms forward and upward, shovel blade rising to chest/shoulder height, small few soil clods leave blade in short arc to right. This frame must clearly differ from frame 5.
7 RETURN: empty shovel lowers diagonally halfway from shoulder back toward ground, elbows bent, torso returns forward, small loose soil fragments gone.
8 SETTLE: empty blade just above ground and arms almost back to frame1, torso halfway forward, seamless loop.
Kneeling stance keeps the same planted boot and knee coordinates in every frame, same character scale, normal adult anatomy, spine bends naturally. Each sprite complete and isolated; no sprite touching adjacent cells, no giant dirt mound or terrain slab underneath. 1-3 tiny soil flecks may appear only during lift/throw. A convincing motion study is more important than decoration.
extraction: Measured transparent content bounds. Preserve generated alpha; nearest-neighbor uniform scaling. All source art is generated, no procedural body, shovel or mine reconstruction.
